tilt: bond duration from the slope of the yield curve
enabled_by: laboratory test L2 (docs/registro-laboratorio-fondo.md): the term spread forecasts the 10-year excess return over bills
question: Would holding the 10-year Treasury only when its yield exceeds the 3-month bill yield, and bills otherwise, have improved the bond sleeve against always holding the 10-year bond?

returns.bond: monthly 10-year par bond by duration approximation GS10(t)/12 - D * (GS10(t+1) - GS10(t))

rule: at each month t hold the bond in month t+1 if GS10(t) > TB3MS(t), otherwise bills
primary_metric: annualized mean monthly return difference (rule minus always-bond)
test: one-sided stationary-block bootstrap of the mean difference, 12-month mean block, 10000 draws, seed 20261115

verdict_rule.supported: difference > 0, p < 0.05 and the rule's maximum drawdown is not worse than always-bond

descriptive_only: Sharpe of each sleeve in excess of bills
effect on the full 70/25/5 mix with US equity from Shiller
if_supported: a registered shadow fund version, never a change to fondo-v2
limits: Monthly average yields, duration approximation, US Treasuries only (AGG also holds mortgages and corporate bonds).
